newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT says to cut international phone rates.
newsitem.headline: PLDT says to cut international phone rates.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co said on Wednesday it was close to an agreement with AT&T Corp on cutting accounting rates from $1.0 a minute to 85 cents.
"We are amenable to the 85 cents and we should have an agreement by end of April," PLDT senior vice-president Antonio Samson told reporters after the company's stockholders' meeting.

Accounting rates refer to the cost of handling calls between a Philipine carrier and its counterpart in other countries. Of the $1.0 per minute charge, half goes to PLDT and the remaining amount to its foreign counterpart.
The United States Federal Communications Commission has said it favours a lowering in accounting rates to 38 cents over the next two years.
Philipine telecommunication firms have opposed the proposal and asked for a deferment in its implementation since this will lead to lower revenues.
"We are probably headed towards 38 cents in the next five years," Samson said.
International long distance revenues accounted for 55.4 percent of PLDT's operating revenues in 1996.
Samson said the reduction in accounting rates will cut dependency on international long distance revenues to 33 percent in five years.
